comparator.name: International Bachelor Communication and Media
comparator.route: Communication, Culture and Society focus area
comparator.sourceNotes: The official three-year, 180-EC English-taught programme combines communication and media theory, social-science research, digital-content practice, focus-area choices, an internship, exchange or minor space, ethics and a bachelor thesis. From year 2 students choose focus areas. Communication, Culture and Society is selected neutrally because it most broadly continues the generic programme identity.
components: Communication and media theory across culture, politics, business and technology
Social-science research, statistics and comparative analysis
Communication, Culture and Society is used for the neutral comparator route.
Digital content, communication management and research workshop
Exchange or minor and elective space
Bachelor thesis class and bachelor thesis

courses: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: Communication and media theory, industries, audiences and technologies
Culture, identity, social change and intercultural communication
Quantitative, qualitative and comparative communication research
Media ethics, representation and creative communication
adjacent: Communication and Politics / International and Global Communication
questions: How do media technologies and institutions shape culture, identity and public life?
How can communication research inform ethical, political and organisational practice?

selection.assessment: The closest curriculum integrates communication, culture, society, media and digital technologies, and it also absorbs the Media and Entertainment and New Media Technologies interests. Political/international communication and organisational/business communication remain coherent official focus directions that UCR can represent with materially distinct curricula. Three alternatives are included, the maximum.

alternatives.label: Communication, culture & digital media
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum connects communication and media to cultural institutions, identity, digital platforms, representation and social change.
alternatives.concept: A broad communication-and-media pathway centred on culture, digital media, audiences, representation and social change.
progression: Introductory media, sociology and art-history courses precede advanced digital media, representation and communication practice. Level-300 seminars are concentrated in later years. All offerings are respected.

alternatives.label: Political, international & public communication
alternatives.labelReason: International relations, comparative politics, conflict and public international law are joined to media, rhetoric and communication research, making public and political communication the organising strand.
alternatives.concept: A political and international communication direction examining media, public debate, global power, conflict, law and persuasive communication.
alternatives.distinctness: This route replaces much of the closest curriculum’s arts, heritage and entertainment-media content with international relations, comparative politics, peace and conflict, public international law and political history.
progression: Law, Society & Justice precedes level-200 and level-300 law. Introductory political, historical and communication courses precede advanced conflict, international relations and research seminars. All offerings are respected.

alternatives.label: Strategic business & organisational communication
alternatives.labelReason: Business foundations, leadership, entrepreneurship, economics and data are integrated with rhetoric and persuasive communication to create a strategic organisational direction.
alternatives.concept: A business-communication direction focused on organisational messaging, leadership, customers, strategy, data and persuasive communication.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the other routes, this curriculum replaces most history, politics and cultural-media study with business, economics, entrepreneurship, leadership, finance and data analysis.
progression: Business, economics, data and communication foundations precede advanced management, leadership, entrepreneurship and econometrics. All formal prerequisites and semester offerings are respected.

notes.text: UCR can form strong interdisciplinary communication pathways but cannot replicate IBCoM’s complete specialist theory-and-methods sequence, designated focus-area menu, required professional internship, international cohort structure or supervised communication thesis programme.

routeSelection.route: Communication, Culture and Society focus area
routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is generic Communication and Media. The official programme offers six focus areas; Communication, Culture and Society most broadly preserves the programme’s core social-science identity and is selected independently of UCR fit.
